title: fleet skills: project memory never restates rules; a dispatch order missing its derivation is sent back; a ruling that disagrees with the skill gets a skill card the same day
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

## Problem

The skill already says rules live in the skill and current values live in the seat post and project memory (`references/filing-gate.md` 22), that memory is a cache and never a ledger (`references/project-forms.md` 29, `references/coordinator.md` 9 and 40), and that a dispatch order goes in the thread's opening message, not a shared folder (`references/dispatch-runbook.md` 130). No line forbids restating a rule in project memory, and no line lets the receiving side send back a dispatch order that lacks its derivation. What that cost:

- A project-memory effort line was a restatement and went stale twice: one version said p1 runs at xhigh, and three card threads were opened at xhigh on it; a later rewrite said epic children and security cards run at xhigh, while `execution-duties.md`'s dispatch section had already moved to the card's own difficulty.
- One seat's card-thread briefs in a shared folder restated a process: card threads then read seven PM files, claimed for themselves and started an `os-dev` sub-agent, the opposite of the `dispatch-runbook.md` card-thread section.

## Ruling

The maintainer ordered this card. The ruling record is the first comment on this card; the PR's `Ruling-ref:` cites it.

## What changes (wording compressed to the byte ratchet; meaning unchanged)

1. `references/project-forms.md`, near line 29 (memory is a cache): project memory holds only the maintainer's words with their time, and pointers into the skill; it ⛔ never restates a rule; a memory line that disagrees with the skill ⇒ follow the skill and delete the line.
2. `references/dispatch-runbook.md`, card-thread section (after line 127, seat and area side): a thread or area that finds its dispatch order missing a derivation ⇒ does not start and sends it back to the seat; ⛔ never fills the tier from memory. Mirror line in `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, since under the lean flow a card thread reads `os-dev.md`, the order and the card, not the skill.
3. `references/project-forms.md`, same place: a maintainer ruling that disagrees with the skill ⇒ a skill card the same day; the memory line names that card and is deleted when it merges; when a skill PR merges, the coordinator reviews memory against the changed lines.

## Constraints

- `.claude/**` is governed: `Rule-change: ruled`, exactly one `Ruling-ref:` line; the L2 record must read `Rule-change-verified: ruled`. A sentence beyond the ruled meaning turns the PR Tier H.
- Byte ratchet at headroom 0 for every file touched: compress the same file first; if it cannot fit, stop and tell the seat the file and the shortfall.
- Per `filing-gate.md` 22-26: no card numbers, comment ids or dated quotes in the skill text.
- Skill text: build tier and L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

## Fold

Item 2 edits the same card-thread section of `dispatch-runbook.md` as #35813 (same mechanism: what a card thread is handed and reads). Both ride one PR, dispatched once #35790 (which holds `dispatch-runbook.md`) merges. Items 1 and 3 avoid `coordinator.md` and `filing-gate.md`, which open PRs hold.

## Not in this card

"Have a script print effort and container, and the coordinator only copies it" conflicts with `references/instrument-discipline.md` 10 (`dispatch-gates.mjs` is frozen; no new derivation rows). It needs its own maintainer ruling.

## Done when

- The three lines (and the `os-dev.md` mirror) are in the skill text, each covered by the ruling.
- `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` passes.
